flashcards.back: The immutable Spirit is God; his nature, with cognition and desire, is Adhyatma; his creative power that brings beings forth is Karma.

flashcards.front: What you think of at the end (8.6)
flashcards.back: Whatever one remembers on leaving the body, one attains, because of constantly thinking of it through life.
Always remember God and do your duty; with mind and intellect fixed on him, you will reach him.
Senses controlled, mind on God, meditating and uttering OM, one reaches the supreme abode.

flashcards.front: Who finds God easy to reach? (8.14)
flashcards.back: The ever-steadfast yogi who always thinks of him, mind going nowhere else.

flashcards.front: Is a heavenly world the end?
flashcards.back: No. All worlds, heaven included, return to rebirth; only reaching God ends it.
Beings come forth again and again at the dawn of Brahma's day and dissolve at his night.
Light, the path of Self-knowledge, leads to liberation; darkness, the path of ignorance, leads to rebirth.

flashcards.front: What surpasses Vedic study, sacrifice and charity?
flashcards.back: The yogi fixed in God goes beyond all their merit and reaches the eternal abode.

quiz.text: According to 8.6, what does one attain after death?

options.A: Whatever one remembers at the end

quiz.why: Constant thought in life shapes the last thought, and the destination.

options.D: Always remember God and do your duty

quiz.text: Who does not return to rebirth?
quiz.why: All other worlds are still subject to rebirth.

quiz.text: What happens at the start of Brahma's day?
The path of light leads to:
quiz.why: 8.26: light of Self-knowledge to salvation; darkness to rebirth.

quiz.text: What does the yogi fixed in God go beyond?

options.D: All merit of Vedas, sacrifice, austerity, charity

quiz.why: Inner union outweighs outer ritual merit.

quiz.text: What sacred sound is uttered when leaving the body in 8.12-13?
quiz.why: OM, the sacred monosyllable, with the mind on God.
